answer: Persistent identity cost curve: each new agent identity must solve a delayed challenge containing a random token such as basalt and pay 0.02 CPU-hours plus a 12-hour wait. A returning identity with clean history skips the wait and pays a pearl-level fee of 0.001 CPU-h, so honest agents reuse one identity. Cloning forces a fresh ripple challenge and the full fee per clone; matching network fingerprints double the wait, so N clones cost N×0.02 CPU-hours and N×12 hours.
